title: Region Surge Prediction and Operator-Guided Failover Playbook
author: Dana Chen
content:
Summary:

This runbook describes operator-guided failover for region-level capacity surges predicted by our ensemble signal. The playbook combines an automated prediction signal (SurgeScore) with human validation steps to reduce false positives and avoid unnecessary cross-region traffic shifts. Target audience: oncall platform engineers and SRE run leads.

Scope and goals:

- Scope: Redwood Inference hosted and dedicated control-plane traffic routing to edge/data-plane regions (cloud regions and peered POPs).
- Goals:
  - Detect high-confidence regional client demand surges before SLOs degrade.
  - Provide step-by-step operator guidance for controlled, reversible failover to secondary regions or burst capacity pools.
  - Preserve token-cost and latency SLOs while minimizing user-visible errors.

Key metrics and SLOs referenced:

- API foreground p50/p95 latency SLOs: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 400ms.
- Token error-rate SLO: < 0.1% request-level errors.
- Region capacity headroom target: >= 15% free GPU slots per shard.

Signals and thresholds (inputs to decision):

- SurgeScore (model-based): probability [0-1].
  - Low: < 0.3 — informational only.
  - Medium: 0.3–0.6 — require human review.
  - High: > 0.6 — trigger oncall paging.
- Region-p95-latency-ratio: p95_region / p95_global > 1.4
- Queue depth growth: 5min growth rate > 30% and sustained 3 measurements
- Scheduler evictions: >= 5 evictions/min over 2 consecutive mins
- Token error spike: 3x baseline in rolling 5m

Dashboards and alerts to consult:

- Dashboards:
  - "Region Health Overview" (Dash ID: PLT-REGION-001) — high-level latency, error-rate, queue depth by region.
  - "Surge Prediction Heatmap" (PLT-PRED-003) — shows SurgeScore across regions and tenants.
  - "Burst Pool Utilization" (PLT-BURST-002) — current burst capacity usage.
  - "Scheduler Evictions and GPU Interference" (PLT-GPU-007).
- Alerts (examples):
  - alert: RegionHighSurgeScore
    expr: surge_score{job="surge-pred"} > 0.6
    runbook: this doc (section: Emergency failover)
  - alert: RegionP95Spike
    expr: increase(region_p95_ratio[5m]) > 0.4
  - alert: QueueDepthGrowthHigh
    expr: rate(api_queue_depth[1m]) > 0.3

Who should be paged:

- Primary: platform-oncall (rotation)
- Secondary: runtime-systems team lead (if infrastructure-level action likely)
- Optional: customer-success for high-profile customers with region affinity (runbook owner to decide)

Preliminary triage (0–10 minutes):

1. Confirm the SurgeScore alert in the prediction dashboard. Note the affected region, tenants, and expected surge duration (model provides 15/60/240m buckets).
2. Validate telemetry: check Region Health Overview for p95/p50, errors, queue depth and evictions.
3. Check scheduled maintenance and deployment slate (Platform Calendar) to rule out planned work.
4. If SurgeScore is Medium (0.3–0.6): run synthetic validation (section: Synthetic validation). If no corroborating signals, monitor and re-evaluate in 10 minutes.

Synthetic validation (commands and queries):

- PromQL sample to validate queue depth vs baseline:
  avg_over_time(api_queue_depth{region="eu-west-1"}[10m]) / avg_over_time(api_queue_depth{region="eu-west-1"}[6h])
- Synthetic request script (kube job):
  kubectl run synth-validate --image=redwood/synth-check:stable --restart=Never -- \
    --target-region eu-west-1 --profile low-latency --qps 5 --duration 60s
- Expected result: < 5% of synthetic requests exceed p95 threshold. If > 20% fail, escalate immediately.

Decision matrix: when to enact operator-guided failover

- Conditions to proceed (need 2/3):
  1) SurgeScore >= 0.6 OR SurgeScore >= 0.45 with sustained p95_ratio > 1.4
  2) Queue growth sustained and scheduler eviction rate high
  3) Synthetic checks confirm > 10% degradation or token error spike
- If 2/3 conditions met, proceed to controlled failover. Otherwise continue monitoring and mitigations (cache warming, prefix caching).

Operator-guided failover steps (controlled):

Estimated duration: 8–25 minutes depending on propagation.

1. Announce on #platform-ops and set incident channel. Post summary: region, SurgeScore, metrics, tentative action.
2. Scale burst pools (noninvasive):
   - CLI: rwoodctl capacity burst-scale --region eu-west-1 --factor 1.5 --reason "Surge validation"
   - Verify burst pool nodes come online in bursts dashboard.
3. If burst scaling insufficient after 3m, prepare traffic shift playbook:
   a. Select target region(s) with capacity headroom (prefer same continent).
   b. Put routing into "guided-failover" mode (no automatic spread):
      - API: curl -X POST $CONTROL_PLANE/api/v1/routing/mode -d '{"mode":"guided","from":"eu-west-1","to":["eu-central-1"]}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
   c. Apply weighted steering: start at 5% traffic shift to target region for top 5 tenants by traffic, monitor for 2 minutes.
   d. Increase in 10% increments every 2 minutes while monitoring p95 and token errors.
4. If target region p95 degrades > 20% over baseline, immediately rollback last increment and reduce weight by 50%.
5. Once 80–90% of non-affinitized traffic is shifted and SLOs are stable, enable routing automation back to normal but keep a conservative rate limit for 30 minutes.

Emergency failover (when SLOs failing and rapid action required):

- Trigger criteria: sustained token error-rate > 0.5% or p95 > 2x baseline for > 3 minutes.
- Steps:
  1) Page leaders and set incident severity to SEV3+.
  2) Execute immediate traffic redirect to fallbacks:
     rwoodctl routing redirect --from eu-west-1 --to eu-central-1 --force --percent 50
  3) Throttle low-priority tenants via soft-quota:
     rwoodctl quota set --tenant <tenant-id> --region eu-west-1 --qps 5
  4) If cross-region redirect causes cost explosion, enable cost-guard: rwoodctl cost-guard --enable --threshold 1.5x
  5) Declare incident and follow incident runbook for customer comms.

Rollback criteria and procedure:

- Rollback if: target region p95 worsens by > 20% or token error-rate increases after shift, or if core infra events are detected in target region.
- Procedure: decrement traffic weights to last known-good state in 2 steps, scale down burst pools if overprovisioned, and restore routing mode to "conservative".

Post-action checklist (within 60m):

- Confirm all tenants have stable latencies and errors.
- Collect the timeline: SurgeScore, synthetic results, routing weight changes, and operator actions. Attach to incident channel.
- Open a short incident report (IR) and tag for retrospective.

Runbook commands and examples (cheat sheet):

- Check SurgeScore (CLI):
  rwoodctl metrics get --name surge_score --region eu-west-1 --window 5m
- Burst-scale example: rwoodctl capacity burst-scale --region eu-west-1 --factor 1.5
- Guided routing mode: curl -X POST $CONTROL_PLANE/api/v1/routing/mode...
- Immediate redirect: rwoodctl routing redirect --from $REG --to $TO --percent 50 --force

Game day and simulation exercises (recommended cadence):

- Quarterly simulation: run a synthetic surge for 120m against a sandbox region. Validate detection, operator playbook timing, and rollback.
- Bi-annual full game day: include customer-success and sales for comms practice.

Known risks and mitigations:

- Cross-region latency penalty: mitigate by preferring same-continent targets and by warming caches in the target region prior to shifting significant traffic.
- Cost runaway: enable cost-guard and monitor burst-pool billing metrics. Pre-authorize spend thresholds with finance for emergency scaling.
- Tenant affinity violations: mark high-affinity tenants in the routing config to avoid shifting critical traffic.

Ownership and escalation contacts:

- Runbook owner: Dana Chen (platform-ops lead) — dana@redwood.ai
- Pager: platform-oncall rotation (Slack alias @platform-oncall)
- Exec escalation: Marco Ruiz (runtime-systems)

Postmortem and continuous improvement:

- For every guided failover, capture a short retrospective within 72 hours with:
  - Root cause hypothesis
  - Which signals were correct/incorrect
  - Time-to-decision metrics and blind spots
  - Action items with owners and due dates

Change history:

- 2025-11-12: Created by Dana Chen.
- 2026-01-09: Updated decision matrix and added SurgeScore thresholds after Q4 simulations.

Appendix: telemetry queries and recommended dashboard panels

- PromQL: surge_score by region -> avg_over_time(surge_score[1m])
- PromQL: region p95 ratio -> histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,region)) / scalar(global_p95_baseline)

Tables (quick references):

| Action | CLI / API | Expected time | Safety check |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Burst-scale | rwoodctl capacity burst-scale --factor X | 1–3m | node ready count > 0 |
| Start 5% shift | routing API POST | 1–2m | target p95 within 10% |
| Increment +10% | routing API POST | 2m | monitor token error-rate |
| Emergency redirect 50% | rwoodctl routing redirect --force | <1m | oncall confirm SEV3 |
